full_judgment: 6. Respondent No.6, Mohammad Ali, contested the rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition and a supplementary affidavit-in-opposition denying the material averments made in the writ petition contending, inter alia, that respondent No.6 is neither a borrower nor a mortgagor of any land with bank and that he had knowledge about the Artha Rin Suit. His father Serajuddin Sarder was the owner of 6 decimals of the land of suit khatian/suit plot. After his death, by amicable partition, amongst his heirs, Mohammad Ali became owner of 0.75 decimal of land and his brothers, Abul Hossain, Rabiul Hossain and Motiur Rahman got 1.75 decimals of land each from the suit khatian/ plot by a registered deed of partition deed 08-09-1986. This respondent had been in possession thereof by mutating his name and paying rent to the Government. By constructing a shop thereon he had been in possession of same through his tenant. All of a sudden on 19-08-2004 the staff of the Adalat, and others came to his land and took over possession thereof forcibly which was not the subject matter of the instant suit. The land owned by him was not mortgaged by his brother but his brother took loan by mortgaging 1.75 decimals of land which is a separate land and not the subject matter of the suit. But at the time of taking over possession of the mortgaged land sold in auction, the auction purchaser in collusion with the Adalat's staff and others dispossessed him from his land illegally, as his land was contiguous to the land sold in auction. As the land claimed by respondent No. 6 is neither mortgaged nor sold in auction, the petitioner did not have the locus standi to file the writ petition. The impugned order is legal and, as such, the rule is liable to be discharged.
